    Fit dispersal kernels

    Source: R/inv-spread.R
    inv_dispersal_kernel.Rd

    Fits one or more distance kernels to observed dispersal distances by maximum likelihood and ranks them by AIC. The kernels describe the probability density of dispersal distance and differ in the weight of their tail: the half-normal is thin-tailed, the exponential has a standard tail and the Weibull (shape below 1), lognormal and gamma can be fat-tailed, which drives accelerating spread.

    Usage

    inv_dispersal_kernel(
  .data,
  distance,
  family = kernel_families(),
  weights = NULL
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per dispersal event.

    distance

    <tidy-select> Column with positive dispersal distances.

    family

    Character vector of kernels to fit: any of "exponential", "halfnormal", "weibull", "lognormal", "gamma".

    weights

    <tidy-select> Optional column of frequency weights (for example, the number of seeds trapped at a distance).

    Value

    An object of class inv_kernel with one fit per family, ordered by AIC. Use tidy() for parameter estimates, glance() for model comparison (log-likelihood, AIC, Akaike weights, mean and 99th percentile dispersal distance), augment() for fitted densities and autoplot() for density and tail plots.

    References

    Nathan, R., Klein, E., Robledo-Arnuncio, J. J. and Revilla, E. (2012). Dispersal kernels: review. In Dispersal Ecology and Evolution, Oxford University Press, 187-210.

    Examples

    k <- inv_dispersal_kernel(
  dplyr::filter(inv_dispersal, species == "sp_a"), distance = distance_m
)
glance(k)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 11
#>   family          n n_par logLik   AIC   BIC delta_AIC   weight mean_distance
#>   <chr>       <int> <int>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 weibull       300     2 -1623. 3250. 3258.       0   9.97e- 1          93.6
#> 2 gamma         300     2 -1629. 3262. 3270.      12.0 2.50e- 3          95.0
#> 3 lognormal     300     2 -1631. 3266. 3274.      15.9 3.44e- 4         140. 
#> 4 exponential   300     1 -1666. 3335. 3338.      84.4 4.75e-19          95.0
#> 5 halfnormal    300     1 -1768. 3537. 3541.     287.  4.99e-63         140. 
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: q99_distance <dbl>, converged <lgl>
tidy(k)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>   family      term     estimate std.error
#>   <chr>       <chr>       <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 weibull     shape     0.690    0.0305  
#> 2 weibull     scale    72.9      6.44    
#> 3 gamma       shape     0.580    0.0396  
#> 4 gamma       rate      0.00610  0.000623
#> 5 lognormal   meanlog   3.48     0.0985  
#> 6 lognormal   sdlog     1.71     0.0697  
#> 7 exponential scale    95.0      5.49    
#> 8 halfnormal  sigma   175.       7.15
